info.name: tibERbu CCE Emitter Adaptor
info.description:
Sample requests for the tibERbu CCE Emitter Adaptor's single inbound endpoint, POST /inbound. Every example body and saved response in this collection was captured against a real, running stack - the adaptor in Docker, wired to the real cce-collector-service (not a stub) - not hand-typed guesses.

## Flow

In production: tibERbu -> CCE Gateway (Basic Auth -> Keycloak token exchange -> JWT validation + authorization) -> this adaptor -> CCE Collector -> Kafka. Folder 1 below exercises that real path end to end. Folders 2-5 bypass the gateway and hit the adaptor directly on its own port - useful for isolating the adaptor's own behavior in isolation, matching the adaptor's own docker-compose.yml dev setup, but not what a real tibERbu call looks like.

## Variables

- `base_url` - the adaptor's own base URL, bypassing the gateway (default: http://localhost:8081)
- `gateway_base_url` - the CCE Gateway's base URL (default: http://localhost:8090)
- `gateway_basic_auth_username` / `gateway_basic_auth_password` - a real Keycloak user in the `cce` realm, holding a realm role the gateway's own api_permissions table maps to POST /inbound. Never the gateway's own client secret - Postman only ever needs to know these two values.
- `patient_id` / `facility_id` - reused across the constructed (non-artifact) example bodies below

## Where the real examples come from

The two full Consent bundles and the Patient-only bundle are copied verbatim from this repo's own artifacts/ folder (real tibERbu sample payloads) - see api-reference.md section 3 for the same examples. artifacts/ is gitignored, so this collection inlines the content directly rather than referencing that path.

item.name: 1. Via CCE Gateway (Basic Auth) - Primary Flow
item.description: The real inbound path: tibERbu -> CCE Gateway (Basic Auth -> Keycloak token exchange -> JWT validation + authorization) -> this adaptor -> CCE Collector. Folders 2-5 below all bypass the gateway and hit the adaptor directly - useful for isolating the adaptor's own behavior, but not what a real tibERbu call looks like.

item.name: 1.1 Consent - via Gateway with Basic Auth

request.description:
This is the real production-shaped flow: Postman sends HTTP Basic Auth credentials (a real Keycloak user, NOT the adaptor's own credentials) straight to the CCE Gateway. The gateway itself exchanges those Basic credentials for a Keycloak access token (OAuth2 resource-owner-password grant, via a dedicated confidential client the gateway holds - Postman never sees that client secret), validates the resulting JWT, checks the caller's realm role against the gateway's own api_permissions table for POST /inbound, and only then forwards the request to the tibERbu adaptor - which forwards it again to the real Collector, exactly as in folder 3.

Requires: BASIC_AUTH_ENABLED=true on gateway-service, a confidential Keycloak client with Direct Access Grants enabled, a POST /inbound route wired to the adaptor with the JwtValidationFilter, and a matching api_permissions row (permission name backed by a realm role the test user holds) - see the adaptor's own docs for exactly how this was set up.

item.name: 1.2 No Authorization Header - Rejected by Gateway

request.description: No Authorization header at all - the gateway rejects it before the request ever reaches the adaptor.
Overall health, including downstream disk/ping indicators.
Kubernetes liveness probe — process is alive.
Kubernetes readiness probe — ready to accept traffic.

Real tibERbu envelope from artifacts/'Consent Payload Structures - Verified Consent.json' - a Patient entry (skipped) plus a fully OTP-verified Consent. Both entries are the exact same resource IDs on every run, so re-sending this request a second time returns collectorStatus: "duplicate" instead of "accepted" (see 2.1b below) - that's the real Collector's own dedup, not a canned response.

request.description: The exact same request as 2.1, sent again. Same deterministic CloudEvents id, so the real Collector reports it as an already-ingested duplicate - still outcome: "forwarded" and still 202, since a duplicate is a successful outcome, just not a new one.

request.description: Real tibERbu envelope from artifacts/'Consent Payload Structures - OTP, Afyayangu, Biometrics.json' - status: "proposed", verification.verified: false. The adaptor forwards this identically to a verified Consent - verification state is business data on the resource, not something the adaptor branches on.

item.name: 3.3 Mixed Outcome - one forwarded, one failed

request.description: A 3-entry bundle: Patient (skipped), a valid Consent (forwards), and an Observation with no patient/subject reference at all (fails with PATIENT_ID_NOT_FOUND). Confirms the multi-entry policy: since at least one entry forwarded, the whole request is still 202 - the failed sibling entry's own reason is still visible in events[], it just doesn't change the overall status.

item.name: 5. Error Responses

request.description: A single Observation entry with no subject/patient reference at all. Since it's the bundle's only candidate entry and it fails outright, there's nothing else to report as a success - the request surfaces as a genuine error instead of a 200/202.

request.description: /inbound only maps POST. Any other method is rejected explicitly as 405, never as 500.

item.description: COLLECTOR_CLIENT_ERROR (4xx from the real Collector) and COLLECTOR_FORWARDING_ERROR (502, retries exhausted) are documented in api-reference.md section 4.5/4.8 but aren't included as runnable requests here - reproducing them needs the real Collector itself to reject or become unreachable, which isn't safe to script against a shared local instance.
